messages.text: I’m assessing a LAr layout that retains the inner3T magnet and tracker, with explicit service corridors and a reserved forward-calorimeter insertion. I’ll separate source geometry from the new envelope and service-budget choices.

The source geometry supports retaining the original barrel sampling radii and removing ALLEGRO’s outer-coil allocation. That avoids changing the absorber spacing or LAr gaps. I’m now sizing the service lanes and end-turn space; a corridor’s cross-sectional area alone does not establish connector or bend access.

I’m using the PDF-reading workflow to verify the cooling and electronics figures in the primary slides. The public PDFs are accessible directly, so the budget can cite the actual pages rather than search snippets.

The cold electronics need a larger reservation than the original40 mm rear bath. With350×75 mm boards and a provisional512 channels per board, explicit packing needs two radial banks in the barrel and three planes behind the endcap. I’ll give the coordinator the channel-capacity formula so these allowances can be revised when the electronics design is fixed.

The explicit packing supports a 140 mm rear barrel bath and a 250 mm rear endcap bath under provisional 512-channel, 35 mm-deep board assumptions. A 700 mm barrel/endcap gap can accommodate the proposed cryogenic bend envelope. The remaining limits are connector and feedthrough footprints, board depth and channel capacity, and qualification of the longer cooling network.

The largest reserved utility pipe changes the gap budget: at 100 mm outer diameter and a provisional bend radius of four diameters, it needs 763 mm for the front S-bend and 470 mm for the rear turn. I recommend 800 mm and 500 mm gaps. Extending the active barrel half-length by 10 mm to 3910 mm keeps its geometric coverage overlapping the shifted endcap within the same 4100 mm reservation.

Input: **`e33ae62ce16592c26c581c5311c4dc493d9714b1`**; comparative assessment read at **`a3dffd327e47cc65dfacb33cf6b7219923683166`**. This is the explicit generic SysArch fallback, with no native profile loading or design acceptance claimed. **Files changed: none.**

I recommend preserving ALLEGRO’s original sampling radii and plane geometry, enlarging the cold electronics baths and external routing gaps. The original coilless **600 mm radial allocation is a lower-bound estimate**: it leaves only the source’s 40 mm rear bath, which is insufficient for the provisional cold-board arrangement below.

A correction to the preliminary gap budget is necessary: **700/400 mm front/rear gaps accommodate the proposed 80 mm nitrogen jackets, but not the larger 100 mm utility pipes. Use 800/500 mm.**

**Sourced geometry and compact alternative**

Official k4geo at **`e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb`** defines barrel sampling **2172.8–2578.3 mm**, inclination **50.18°**, **1536 planes**, **11 layers**, 1.8 mm Pb, 0.1 mm total steel, 0.1 mm total glue, 1.2 mm PCB and nominal **2×1.246 mm LAr gap**. Its 70 mm rear term includes ALLEGRO’s integrated outer solenoid; its 49 mm air margins are placeholder gaps. Preserve the nODD inner 3 T magnet and remove the imported outer-coil allocation and XML’s separate 2 T field assumption. [Pinned barrel XML](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb/FCCee/ALLEGRO/compact/ALLEGRO_o1_v03/ECalBarrel_thetamodulemerged.xml#L20)

For a compact warm front at 1700 mm, retaining the same front closures gives active \(R=1772.8\) mm. The approximate front normal pitch,

\[
p_n=2\pi R\cos(50.18^\circ)/1536,
\]

falls from **5.692 to 4.644 mm**. After the 3.2 mm absorber/PCB stack, only **1.444 mm** remains for the double LAr gap—approximately **42% less** than the source gap. Preserving pitch instead requires approximately **1253 planes**, with new segmentation and absorber geometry. This is a redesign, not passive repackaging.

**Concrete unsigned prototype**

All following dimensions are **nODD design choices**, in mm. Radii are circular unless explicitly marked as polygon apothems.

| Assembly/interface | Proposed allocation |
|---|---:|
| Barrel active sampling | \(R=2172.8–2578.3,\ |z|\le3910\) |
| Barrel warm assembly | \(R=2100–2800,\ |z|\le4100\) reservation |
| Existing magnet reservation → barrel front | \(2100-1640=\mathbf{460}\) radial |
| Barrel rear cold bath | **140** |
| Barrel → HCAL external radial corridor | \(R=2800–3100:\ \mathbf{300}\) |
| Barrel/endcap external axial gap | \(|z|=4100–4900:\ \mathbf{800}\) |
| Endcap active blades | \(R=410–2790,\ |z|=5010–5460\) |
| Endcap warm assembly | \(R=301–2949,\ |z|=4900–5860\) |
| Endcap rear cold bath | **250** |
| HCAL barrel | Front apothem **3100**, cover outer apothem **4595.9**, half-length **5860** |
| HCAL barrel maximum corner radius | **4685.939** for 16 sides |
| Rear ECAL → HCAL endcap gap | \(|z|=5860–6360:\ \mathbf{500}\) |
| HCAL endcap | \(R_\mathrm{inner}=300\), outer apothem **4585.9**, \(|z|=6360–7855.9\) |

The HCAL depth remains \(36(30+10.275+1)+10=\mathbf{1495.9}\) mm, taken from the pinned nODD input. Increasing its radius and length changes aggregate mass and magnet interfaces; those require the coordinator’s implementation audit.

The barrel radial sequence is **10 warm wall +49 separation +3.8 cold wall +10 front bath +405.5 sampling +140 rear bath +30 cold wall +49 separation +2.7 warm wall =700 mm**. The axial closure is 100 mm cold access +3.8 cold wall +49 separation +30 warm wall; with active half-length3910, the physical outer half-length is **4092.8**, inside the4100 reservation.

For the endcap, preserve the source’s constructed blades and support tubes, rather than the misleading nominal bath boundary. Its source rear support already occupies **10 mm gap +30 mm rings/spokes**. [Pinned turbine XML](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb/FCCee/ALLEGRO/compact/ALLEGRO_o1_v03/ECalEndcaps_Turbine_o1_v03.xml#L15), [construction driver](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb/detector/calorimeter/ECalEndcap_Turbine_o1_v03_geo.cpp#L781)

The endcap envelope above uses **100 front closure +10 front bath +450 active depth +250 rear bath +150 rear closure**. It provisionally preserves the source’s 50/100 mm Al-equivalent closure budgets, inserts separate49 mm vacuum gaps, and splits cold/warm wall material. These are effective prototype allocations, not engineered vessel walls.

**Explicit cold-board packing**

The July2025 thermal drawing provides a **350×75 mm board-face precedent**. It does **not** establish512-channel capacity, connector clearance or35 mm package depth. These remain unsigned hypotheses. [July2025 mechanics/cooling presentation, thermal-layout slides]([external URL redacted; see source journal])

Use provisional \(C_\mathrm{FEB}=512\), board pitch **355×80 mm**, 16 azimuthal service sectors, and independent stations at each barrel end.

- **Barrel:** at bank inner radius2593.3, 20 mm side setbacks allow **12 tangent columns**. Each half supports **10 axial rows**; one explicit grid has board extents \(|z|=102.5–3647.5\). Two banks provide **7680 slots**. Approximately2.3M channels need4493 boards, **58.5% occupancy**; a3M-channel budget needs5860, **76.3% occupancy**.
- **Barrel bath140:** 15 termination +35 board bank +10 separation +35 second bank +5 spreader +22 nitrogen-pipe envelope +18 access.
- **Endcap:** six radial rows starting410,765,1120,1475,1830,2185, with respectively **1,3,5,6,8,10 boards per wedge**, provide **528 slots per plane**. The outer row ends2535, leaving255 mm to the blade envelope.
- The pinned readout constants imply **601600 logical endcap cells per side**. Three512-channel planes provide811008-channel capacity. Parameterically,
  \[
  n_\mathrm{planes}=\left\lceil N_E/(528C_\mathrm{FEB})\right\rceil.
  \]
  At601600–650000 channels,1024-channel boards need two planes;2048-channel boards need one.
- **Endcap bath250:** 40 existing rear mechanics +3×35 banks +2×10 separation +5 spreader +22 pipe +58 access.

These checks establish face packing under the stated package assumptions. They do not establish connector/header routes through boards, support rings or vessel walls.

**Parameterized services and route capacity**

Planning budgets: \(N_B=3\)M channels, \(N_E=650000\) per endcap, eight boards per aggregator. Use **32 barrel stations** and **16 stations per endcap**.

| Per-station reserve | Barrel | Endcap |
|---|---:|---:|
| Boards / aggregators |184 /23|80 /10|
| Shielded differential pairs,2.5 mm OD |92|40|
| Warm fibres,2 mm OD, including100% spare |92|40|
| HV leads,3 mm OD |12|20|
| Power cables,12 mm envelope |4|4|
| Ground/shield cables,8 mm OD |2|2|
| Controls,3 mm OD |4|4|

HV counts assume provisional16-electrode groups, two polarities and barrel feeds from both ends. HV voltage, insulation and actual electrode-feed topology remain unresolved.

Add two **80 mm nitrogen jacket envelopes** and two25 mm warm-rack water pipes per station. With

\[
A_\mathrm{required}=\sum n_i\pi d_i^2/(4f),\quad f=0.40,
\]

the required area is **31104 mm²/barrel station** and **30199 mm²/endcap station**. A **700×150 mm lane** provides105000 mm².

Reserve one enlarged utility lane per detector end containing four additional **100 mm LAr fill/return/purge/relief envelopes**. Its calculated requirement is **109644 mm²**; **1100×150 mm** provides165000 mm². These utility functions and diameters are capacity reservations, not selected plumbing.

At the narrow endcap/HCAL neck, \(R=2949–3100\) gives151 mm radial depth. A16-sector wedge with20 mm side setbacks permits **1133 mm tangent width**, so the1100 mm utility lane fits in local facet coordinates. The utility pipes, nitrogen pair and cable/water tray also admit a side-by-side conceptual arrangement. Flange and manifold shapes remain missing.

A continuous route exists through the **empty external annulus**, past the endcap, into the500 mm rear gap, then radially beyond HCAL where the barrel ends at5860. Every cryostat penetration must have explicit openings, seals and endpoint fittings. The source’s LAr-filled service placeholders cannot be counted as routed cables or empty ports. [Pinned inclined barrel driver](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb/detector/calorimeter/ECalBarrel_NobleLiquid_InclinedTrapezoids_o1_v03_geo.cpp#L118)

For bend allowance, take provisional \(R_\mathrm{bend}=4D\) and20 mm installation clearance. A radial shift324 mm from barrel pipe centre2686 to outside-endcap centre3010 needs

\[
L_S=2\sqrt{R_\mathrm{bend}\Delta R-\Delta R^2/4}+D+20.
\]

This gives **656.55 mm for80 mm pipes** and **762.98 mm for100 mm pipes**. A rear90° turn requires respectively **380/470 mm**. Hence **800/500 mm**. Supplier bend limits and flange/tool access remain unverified.

**Power, cooling and data limits**

The July2025 study gives a **120 kW CFEB scenario**, two-phase nitrogen around86 K, **1.07 kg/s**, and a preliminary **48×6 m×18 mm-ID** calculation below0.03 bar. It explicitly excludes global cooling design. The same presentation also contains a96-half-pipe thermal arrangement; these scenarios must not be merged as qualified hardware. [July2025 presentation, cooling slides20 and44–47]([external URL redacted; see source journal])

Use120 kW barrel plus **40 kW per endcap** as a200 kW planning reserve. Scaling the source enthalpy scenario gives approximately **1.783 kg/s total**, but does not qualify longer branches, manifolds or pressure drop. A provisional192-branch allocation would be96 barrel half-branches plus48 per endcap.

At48 V and90% efficiency, barrel station current is **86.8 A**. Two parallel25 mm² copper supply/return pairs give43.4 A per pair. With a20 m loop and room-temperature copper resistivity \(1.72×10^{-8}\ \Omega m\), calculated drop is **0.60 V** and loss **51.8 W/station**. Cold conversion, startup and fault protection remain open.

For data, \(R=Nf_\mathrm{hit}b_\mathrm{hit}\). At hypothetical simultaneous50 kHz/channel and64 bits/hit,3M channels produce **9.6 Tb/s**;4096-channel aggregation produces13.1 Gb/s. Four5 Gb/s electrical links and two10 Gb/s fibres provide arithmetic capacity before overhead. The source50 kHz figure is a developing CALOROC capability, not demonstrated detector occupancy. [January2026 readout slide11]([external URL redacted; see source journal])

Warm one-cable-per-channel routing is much harder: even an assumed1.2 mm OD requires **176715–265072 mm²/station** for2–3M barrel channels at40% fill. The20k-wire feedthrough R&D would imply **4–5 feedthroughs per station**, without proving flange fit. The September14 W/board example and January<10 mW/channel analog scenario are separate estimates, not interchangeable full-chain totals. [September2025 summary, slides12 and38]([external URL redacted; see source journal])

**Forward reservation and coverage limits**

Reserve a forward EM collar **\(R=80–450,\ |z|=4400–4850\)** and an FCal insertion **\(R=80–290,\ |z|=4850–7855.9\)**. These are empty technology reservations. They leave11 mm radial clearance to the endcap warm bore and10 mm to the HCAL aperture. Anη4 ray reaches **287.87 mm** at the downstream limit, inside the reservation with only2.13 mm margin. The pinned beam pipe ends at4 m; downstream beam-pipe, machine and shielding interfaces are missing.

The3910 mm barrel choice gives any-hit coverage toη1.35021; the shifted endcap begins atη1.34835. Their envelopes overlap, but full barrel radial sampling ends nearη1.20388 and full endcap depth starts nearη1.42423. **The transition therefore requires measured sampling/material response; geometric overlap is not containment.**

Ownership: SysArch coordinates tracker/MagSys↔ECAL envelopes, ECAL mechanics↔readout/cryogenics ports, ECAL↔HCAL service gaps, and FCal↔interaction-region reservations. SoftEng must encode matching frames, circular/polygon conventions, explicit wall openings and material-bearing services. MagSys must reassess the enlarged HCAL steel and retained3 T field.

Actual checks: exact-revision `git show` inputs; fresh pinned official-source retrieval and hashes; actual PDF extraction plus thermal-drawing inspection; standard-library board containment/capacity, bundle areas, electrical-drop, bend and envelope calculations. **No native geometry jobs, dependency changes or source edits.** Missing evidence remains board thickness/channel capacity, headers, flange CAD, mechanical access, vessel design, hydraulic network, downstream beam interfaces and detector response. The pinned source manifest contains no ALLEGRO entries; the coordinator should catalogue these sources with the implementation.
